questions.stemHtml: A male child was brought in Casualty with previous history of URTI and headache. He currently has fever, fatigue and pain on walking for which USG and joint aspiration were done before giving antibiotics. A lytic lesion was seen on the lower end of the femur. The peripheral smear shows the following finding. What is the most probable organism that can be isolated from the joint aspirate?
questions.solutionHtml:
Salmonella
  • Given case is a typical scenario of acute Osteomyelitis in a sickle cell anemia patient.
    • Staphylococcus aureus is the most common causative organism (overall)
  • However, in cases of sickle cell anemia –salmonella is the most common causative organism and hence, A is the correct choice.


Apley’s textbook of Orthopaedics and Trauma 10th edition, PAGE NO. 30-41

questions.stemHtml: An Alcoholic patient presented with white patches in the oral cavity as shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leukoplakia
  • The most commonly described premalignant oral lesions are leukoplakia, Erythroplakia, lichen planus, and submucous fibrosis. Hence, it is essential to differentiate between these lesions.
  • The given image shows oral mucosal white patches with malignancy potential that cannot be scraped off which is a significant pointer for oral Leukoplakia.
  • Associated conditions: squamous cell carcinoma

Risk factors:

  • Tobacco use
  • Alcohol use  
  • Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection
  • Histopathology of oral leukoplakia often reveals hyperkeratosis or parakeratosis with varying degrees of inflammation. Hyperplastic epithelium may be present, in addition to mild, moderate, or severe dysplasia. 

Differentials:

  • Oral hairy leukoplakia
    • Differentiating factors: seen in immunocompromised patients and caused by Epstein-Barr virus
  • Pseudomembranous candidiasis]
  • Differentiating factors: can be scraped off


Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery, 27th Edition, Page Number: 706

questions.stem: A 20 year female working in a school in a rural area developed rice watery diarrhea. The organism responsible for this condition acts via which receptor?
questions.solutionHtml:
GM 1 Gangliosidase Receptor
  • MOA of cholera toxin: GM 1 ganglioside receptor
  • GM1 has important physiological properties and impacts neuronal plasticity and repair mechanisms, and the release of neurotrophins in the brain.
  • Besides its function in the physiology of the brain, GM1 acts as the site of binding for both cholera toxin and E. coli heat-labile enterotoxin (Traveller's diarrhea).


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 964

questions.stem: A Farmer presented with multiple sinuses with a discharging granule on the leg. The granules were crushed and examined. Which of the following statements is correct regarding this scenario?

options.label: A
options.text: Can be caused by Bacteria and Fungi

options.label: B
options.text: Involve Skin only. No Deeper Tissue Involvement

questions.answerText: Can be caused by Bacteria and Fungi
questions.solutionHtml:
Can be caused by Bacteria and Fungi
  • Mycetoma mycetes or Madhura foot is caused by fungal and bacterial infection.
  • These bacteria and fungi may enter the body through a break in the skin, often on a person’s foot.
  • The resulting infection causes firm, usually painless but debilitating masses under the skin that can eventually affect the underlying bone.
  • Clinical features include chronic subcutaneous swelling (option B)
  • Bacterial: Actinomycetes
    • Yellow granules - Actinomadura madurae (MC), Actinomyces, nocardia.
    • Red granules seen in Actinomadura pelletri
  • Fungal: Eumycetoma
    • Black granules- Madurella mycetomatis
    • White granules-Pseudallescheria boydii
  • Involves skin and subcutaneous tissues
  • Lymphocyte accumulation is absent (option C), no lymph drainage and so accumulation may lead to osteolytic lesion.
  • Direct invasion is seen, no hematogenous spread (option D).
  • The treatment for mycetoma depends on whether it is caused by bacteria (actinomycetoma) or fungi (eumycetoma).
  • Actinomycetoma is usually treatable with antibiotics, and surgery is usually not needed.
  • Eumycetoma is usually treated with long-term antifungal medicine, but treatment may not be completely effective. In this case, surgery or amputation are sometimes needed to cut away the infected tissue.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 604

questions.stem: A woodworker presented with chronic localised infection of the skin on lower legs and feet which are irregular, rough, cauliflower like lesions. Microscopy of biopsy shows copper penny bodies. What is the etiological agent?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chromoblastomycosis
  • Chromoblastomycosis aka Verrucous Dermatitis is caused by wood prick. Involves skin and subcutaneous tissues forming warty lesions
  • Biopsy will reveal brown colored globose bodies ,sclerotic bodies or medlar bodies which shows copper penny appearance.



Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 605

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best way to diagnose a clostridium associated diarrhea?
questions.solutionHtml:
Toxin Demonstration
  • DIAGNOSIS The diagnosis of CDI is based on a combination of clinical criteria: (1) diarrhea (≥3 unformed stools per 24 h for ≥2 days) with no other recognized cause plus (2) detection of toxin A or B in the stool, detection of toxin-producing C.
  • difficile in the stool by nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT; e.g., polymerase chain reaction [PCR]) or by culture, or visualization of pseudomembranes in the colon.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, TABLE No. 129-1

questions.stem: A 24 yr old male who recently returned from Africa reported with jaundice and hemorrhagic fever. Histology reveals the presence of Torres bodies. Symptomatic treatment was given but the patient died. Which strain of the vaccine must have prevented this occurrence?
questions.solutionHtml:
17D Strain
  • Above case points to the diagnosis of Yellow fever.
  • The yellow fever virus is an Arbovirus of the Flavivirus genus and is transmitted by Aedes species of mosquitoes.
  • 17D strain Vaccine is a live attenuated vaccine developed for yellow fever.


    • Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 528

questions.stem: A military person in a crowded military basement presented with rash on body, sparing palms and soles. On examination lice found on examination. What is the probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pediculosis Corporis
  • Pediculosis corporis is caused by body lice.
  • Unlike head and pubic lice, body lice do not live on the skin but rather live and lay their eggs in stitches of clothing or bedding, moving to the skin only to feed.
  • Hence in a military person palm and soles are spared. 


Rook's Textbook of Dermatology, 9th Edition, Page No. 38.2, 38.15, 38.16, 38.21–2

questions.stem: A 30 year old military jawan complains of fever, vomiting, rash and myalgia. Similar complaints are found in others. There was an absence of rash in palms and soles. All were suffering from an infestation of lice. What is the causative agent of this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Rickettsia Prowazeki
  • Louse infestation is found in Epidemic typhus and trench fever
  • Sparing of palms and soles is characteristic of epidemic typhus


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 412

questions.stem: A person got admitted in the hospital for sepsis treated with antibiotics for long term, manifested with diarrhea and dehydration. Which investigation is preferred ?
questions.solutionHtml:
GDH Ag and Exotoxins
  • Long term treatment with antibiotics points to Clostridium difficile.
  • Glutamate dehydrogenase enzyme Ag and exotoxins are used to determine C. difficile infection.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 191-192.

questions.stem: A patient presented with annular lesions and central clearing on axilla. Culture on SDA revealed whitish flat to slightly raised colonies showing Red pigment producing pencil shaped Macroconidia. What is the most likely causative organism ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Trichophyton Rubrum
  • Trichophyton rubrum is a dermatophytic fungus in the phylum Ascomycota. It is an exclusively clonal, anthropophilic saprotroph that colonizes the upper layers of dead skin, and is the most common cause of athlete's foot, fungal infection of nail, jock itch, and ringworm worldwide.
  • The colonies are velvety and contain deep red velvety pigment on their reverse side.
  • Trichophyton rubrumgrows slowly in culture with sparse production of teardrop or peg-shaped microconidia laterally on fertile hyphae.
  • Macroconidia, when present, are smooth-walled and narrowly club-shaped, although most isolates lack macroconidia.
  • Growth is inhibited in the presence of certain sulfur-, nitrogen- and phosphorus-containing compounds.
  • Pencil shaped macroconidia are typically seen.
  • Approximately 80–93% of chronic dermatophyte infections in many parts of the developed world are thought to be caused by  rubrumincluding cases of tinea pedis(foot), tinea unguium(nail), tinea manum (hand), tinea cruris(groin), and tinea corporis(arms and leg), as well as some cases of tinea barbae(beard). 
  • Trichophyton rubrum has also been known to cause folliculitis in which case it is characterized by fungal element in follicles and foreign body giant cells in the dermis.




Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 601

questions.stemHtml: A HIV patient presented with fever, cough and breathlessness. The isolated organism was a fungi showing yeast form at 37 C and mould form at 25 C as shown in the image. What is the causative agent?
questions.solutionHtml:
Talaromyces Marneffi
  • Talaromycosis is an infection caused by the fungus Talaromyces marneffei.
  • the image is suggestive of Talaromyces
  • marneffeiused to be called Penicillium marneffei, and talaromycosis used to be called penicilliosis.  Talaromycosis affects people who live in or visit Southeast Asia, southern China, or eastern India. 
  • usually associated with HIV/AIDS, or another immunocompromised condition.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 609

questions.stemHtml: A truck driver manifested with pneumonia. Sample histopathology showed septate hyphae with dichotomous branching (acute angle branching) at 45o as shown in the image. What is the causative organism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aspergillus

Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 609

questions.solutionHtml:
Chromagar

Different species of candida shows different color

questions.stem: A patient presented with a complaint of fever, sore throat and calf pain for one week. On examination he has jaundice, subconjunctival suffusion and tender hepatomegaly. There is no history of travel however he is a sewer worker. No history of chills, rigors and anorexia. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leptospirosis
  • Given a history of fever, sore throat and especially calf pain with a history of sewer worker points to Leptospirosis .
  • Leptospirosis affects multiple organs if left untreated and can cause liver damage, kidney damage and eventually death.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 390
